The '''Players Committee organization''' is the structure of advocates and volunteer teams through which the [[Players Committee]] (PC) runs the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game. This article follows the PC's own organization chart, a one-page PDF (&ldquo;Star Wars CCG Players Committee &ndash; Organization Chart&rdquo;) published on starwarsccg.org. The version used here was created on '''6 May 2024''' and is the version published as of 10 October 2026.<ref name="chart">PC Organization Chart, [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010210152/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf Wayback Machine capture of 10 October 2026] of [https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf] (PDF creation date 6 May 2024; file last modified 6 May 2024). Earlier version: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211005193353/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf Wayback Machine, captured 5 October 2021].</ref>

[[File:Players Committee organization chart 2024.png|thumb|center|1000px|alt=Players Committee organization chart: the Lead Advocate at top, six advocates beneath, and colour-coded volunteer teams below each|The Players Committee organization chart (PDF created 6 May 2024), from the archived copy.<ref name="chart" />]]

== Overview ==

The chart places the Lead Advocate at the top, with six advocates below, each directly over one or more groups of volunteers. Each advocate's box and the team boxes beneath it share a colour: yellow and blue for the Rules Advocate (Rules and Technology), orange for Marketing, gray for Design and Production, green for Tournaments and light blue for Communications. Two further roles, Legal and PC Store Manager, are shown beside the Lead Advocate. Each person is shown with a title and a forums handle; handles appear below in quotation marks. Some volunteers belong to more than one team and are listed under each; in all the chart names 66 individuals. Each advocate has a role address at starwarsccg.org (rules@, marketing@, design@, production@, tournaments@ and communications@).<ref name="chart" /> Current and past advocates are listed on [[Players Committee advocates]].

== Lead Advocate ==

[[Scott Lingrell]] (&ldquo;advocate&rdquo;). Shown beside the Lead Advocate are '''Legal''', [[Casey Anis]] (&ldquo;spideyguy0&rdquo;), and '''PC Store Manager''', [[Chris Gogolen]] (&ldquo;gogolen&rdquo;).

== Rules Advocate ==

[[Greg Zinn]] (&ldquo;Gergall&rdquo;) is over the Rules team and the Technology team.

=== Rules ===

The chart lists the Rules team's work as issuing rulings and clarifying errata to support new gameplay mechanics and correct problems; maintaining the Advanced Rulebook and the Current Rulings forum thread; and answering questions in the Rules forum.

* [[Tim Simon]] (&ldquo;Aglets&rdquo;); [[Hayes Hunter]] (&ldquo;Hayes&rdquo;); [[Stephen Fulner]] (&ldquo;fungineer&rdquo;)

=== Technology ===

Responsibilities: administering [[GEMP]] (online play, programming and development); managing resources such as vKit and Scomp Link Access; overseeing and designing website infrastructure and maintenance; and troubleshooting technology issues in the community.

* '''Lead GEMP Slicer:''' [[Jeremy DiPaolo]] (&ldquo;jdipaolo1&rdquo;)
* '''GEMP team:''' [[Jared Greenwald]] (GEMP Slicer, &ldquo;Jetsaredim&rdquo;); [[Tom Marlin]] (GEMP Slicer, vKit, JSON, Scomp Link, &ldquo;hyvee_doughboy&rdquo;); [[Christian McCarty]] (GEMP Infrastructure, &ldquo;ketura&rdquo;); [[Kevin Standridge]] (GEMP Bots Admin, &ldquo;laforge27&rdquo;)
* '''Infrastructure and apps:''' [[Jason Riendeau]] (Server Infrastructure, &ldquo;Apollyon&rdquo;); [[Ron Howe]] (Holotable CDF Maintainer, &ldquo;ronhowe&rdquo;); [[Scott Atkins]] (Comlink (Android) App. Dev. &amp; Admin., &ldquo;scottrick49&rdquo;); [[Lee Edwards]] (Holocron (iOS) App. Developer &amp; Admin., &ldquo;terron&rdquo;); [[Eric Lanz]] (Epic Duel Developer, &ldquo;New GEMP UI&rdquo;, &ldquo;elanz&rdquo;)

== Marketing Advocate ==

[[Jared Napolitano]] (&ldquo;Jnapolit31&rdquo;) is over the Prize Support, Social Media and Streaming teams. Responsibilities: managing the PC's social media platforms (Twitter, Twitch, Facebook, Slack, Discord, Instagram and YouTube); generating and distributing prize support; streaming and commentating in-person and online events; cultivating new and returning players; administering the annual Donations Program; outreach to cohort organizations; working with the Tournament Committee on prize support; and community-building initiatives.

== Design Advocate ==

[[Chris Kelly]] (&ldquo;chriskelly&rdquo;) is over the Design and Development, Proofing, Playtesting and Competitive Balance teams. == Tournament Advocate ==

[[Chris Schoenthal]] (&ldquo;imrahil327&rdquo;) is over the Tournament Committee, the Decklist Scribe Team, the Jawa Council and the league and event organizers. Responsibilities: organizing and running in-person and online competitive and casual events; addressing competitive play interactions and setting tournament guidelines; maintaining and distributing the Tournament Guide; generating new event concepts, such as formats beside Standard and Open; improving key tournament processes; and keeping gameplay record books and history.

== Communications Advocate ==

[[Keith Brown]] (&ldquo;darkjediknight11&rdquo;) is over the forums moderators. Responsibilities: working with Marketing to convey significant news to the community; administering and summarizing periodic Player Surveys; and moderating the forums while seeking to improve their layout and functionality.

* '''Forums moderators:''' [[Jerry Heine]] (Lead Forums Moderator, &ldquo;quesosauce37&rdquo;); [[Garrett Larson]] (Forums Moderator, &ldquo;deadbody&rdquo;); [[Kyle Krueger]] (Forums Moderator, &ldquo;Meto&rdquo;)

== Notes ==

* Some volunteers appear in more than one team, as on the chart.
* The chart gives approximate sizes for three teams only: Streaming (about 20 members), Playtesting (about 50) and the Competitive Balance Team (about 12).
* The chart's key reads &ldquo;Volunteer Name / Title / Forums Handle&rdquo;.
